_comment: Golden fixtures: one sentence, several actions (PLAN-metalstorm-command-language.md §1 'actions 0..4; multi-step = ordered list'). Order matters — the executor runs them in sequence, and a clarification raised part-way STOPS the rest rather than half-finishing a plan whose premise is in doubt.

fixtures.name: an order plus the guidance that backs it
fixtures.utterance: Chimera Squad take Fallow Gate, and make it a priority for the AI

expected.say: Chimera Squad is taking Fallow Gate, and the AI will prioritise it.

fixtures.name: two squads, two places
fixtures.utterance: Chimera holds Northgate, Ironback takes Osprey Fen

fixtures.name: stance, then a rename, then an order
fixtures.utterance: go aggressive, call Chimera Squad Hammerfall, and send them at Slag Forge
fixtures.note: Three kinds in one envelope. The rename lands before the order, and the order still resolves by the OLD name — the index only learns 'Hammerfall' on the next org-group snapshot, and pretending otherwise would make the third action fail intermittently.

fixtures.name: a mid-plan ambiguity stops the plan
fixtures.utterance: go defensive, then send Chimera to Northgate
fixtures.note: Action 1 (stance) lands; action 2 can't resolve 'Chimera' between two squads, so it asks and the run ends there. What already happened is reported; nothing is guessed.

fixtures.name: a refusal part-way stops the plan and names what was skipped
fixtures.utterance: prioritise Northgate, patrol Slag Forge, and hold Osprey Fen
fixtures.note: M5 changed this from M1's 'a refusal does not stop the plan'. A multi-step envelope is one sentence split up, and its steps lean on each other — running step 3 on the assumption that step 2 happened is how a plan half-executes into a position nobody asked for. Skipping is recoverable; an order sent on a false premise costs authority and moves an army. The stop line names the step that ran and the one that didn't.

fixtures.name: an order and a panel, in the order they were said
fixtures.utterance: defend Northgate and show me the minimap
fixtures.note: M5 acceptance 2. Two kinds in one sentence, and the ORDER is the assertion: the directive commits before the panel opens, because that is the order the player said them in and because a panel that opened first would be the visible half of a sentence whose other half then refused.

expected.say: Defending Northgate, and opening the minimap.

fixtures.name: several named forces become several actions, not one merged name
fixtures.utterance: send Chimera and Basilisk to Fallow Gate
fixtures.note: Prompt rule 6, and the resolver-ambiguity item M5 scoped: `NLCommandIntent.subject` holds ONE subject, so a multi-subject sentence is expressed as multi-step. The alternative — a subject naming 'Chimera and Basilisk' — would be a group that does not exist and could only ever refuse. Note Basilisk is tasked and goes anyway: the player named it, so there is nothing to choose and nothing to ask.

expected.say: Sending Chimera Squad and Basilisk Squad to Fallow Gate.

fixtures.name: more named forces than an envelope can hold is a refusal
fixtures.utterance: send Chimera, Basilisk, Warhound, Kestrel and Ironback to Fallow Gate
fixtures.note: Five subjects, four actions. Refused rather than silently truncated to four — a sentence that moved four of the five armies you named, without saying which one it left behind, is the worst possible outcome of the multi-subject rule.

actions.reason: That's five squads in one order — I can take four at a time. Say it in two.

fixtures.name: the step that fails is named, and the rest is not run
fixtures.utterance: defend the grain silo, then push on to the ridge, then show me the minimap
fixtures.note: The plan's own example of the M5 report: 'defended the silo; couldn't find the ridge'. 'The ridge' is in no index, so step 2 refuses by name and step 3 never happens — the minimap does NOT open, because a panel opening at the end of a plan that failed in the middle reads as success.

saysLike: don't know a place called "the ridge"

fixtures.name: a first step that fails takes the whole plan with it
fixtures.note: The boundary case of the same rule: nothing ran, so the summary says so rather than listing an empty 'did:'. And `say` is never printed — an envelope that achieved nothing acknowledges nothing.

saysLike: nothing ran — stopped there; not run: hold Northgate

fixtures.name: the four-action ceiling
fixtures.utterance: lock Chimera, lock Basilisk, cap AI spending at 150, and go defensive
fixtures.note: MAX_ACTIONS is 4 (plan §1 '0..4'). A longer list is a runaway model, not a plan, and the validator rejects it — so this fixture also pins the boundary as VALID.
